title: Numbers on a line
goal: Put an integer on the line, and say −n as "minus n".
generalHint: Look at the line again. Minus numbers are on the left of 0, and plus numbers are on the right.

screens.label: PUZZLE
screens.title: Two below zero
screens.prompt: A ruler starts at 0. Drag the ring to "2 below zero".

answer.correctWhy: Two below zero is 2 units to the left of 0. We write it as −2.

mistakes.reply: That is 2 above zero. A number below zero is on the other side of 0. Which side is that?

hints: Numbers below zero are on the left of 0.
screens.caption: Drag the orange ring, then check.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: The line turns upright
screens.prompt: The line now stands up. It is a thermometer. It is 3° outside. The temperature falls by 8°. Guess where it stops.

sameSide.correctWhy: The first 3° take the temperature to 0°. The last 5° take it below zero.

otherSide.correctWhy: The temperature falls by more than 3°, so it goes past 0°. 3 − 8 = −5.

screens.caption: Drag the orange ring, then check.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: The line becomes a timeline
screens.prompt: Now the line lies down again. It is a timeline. Each step is 100 years. In Lang's convention, the year −500 is 500 BC. Drag the ring to the year −500.

answer.correctWhy: Step 5 to the left of 0 is 500 years before the year 0. This is 500 BC.

mistakes.reply: That is the year 500 AD. Years before 0 are on the other side. Which side is that?

hints: Years before 0 are on the left of 0.
Each step is 100 years. Make 5 steps.
screens.caption: Each step is 100 years.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Naming the numbers
screens.prompt: The numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, ... are the natural numbers. The point 0 is the origin. Numbers to its left, such as −1, −2, ..., are the negative integers. All of them together are the integers.

interaction.question: Which number is an integer but is not a natural number?

options.reply: 0 is a natural number here. Lang counts 0, 1, 2, ... as the natural numbers. Which number is left of 0?
7 is a natural number. A natural number is on the right of 0, or is 0. Which number is on the left?

feedback.correctWhy: −3 is left of the origin, so it is an integer but not a natural number.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 1 OF 5
screens.title: Put −4 on the line

answer.correctWhy: −4 is 4 units to the left of 0.

mistakes.reply: Minus numbers are on the other side of 0. Which side is that?

hints: Minus numbers are on the left of 0.
Count 4 units to the left of 0.

steps.text: Start at 0. Move 4 units to the left.

answer.correctWhy: −2 is 2 units to the left of 0.

screens.caption: Drag the orange ring, then check.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 2 OF 5
screens.title: Put 0 on the line
screens.prompt: Put 0 on the number line. This point is the origin.

answer.correctWhy: 0 is the origin. It is not left or right of itself.

mistakes.reply: That is 2 units to the right of the origin. Where is the origin?
That is 2 units to the left of the origin. Where is the origin?

hints: The origin is the point where the ruler starts.

steps.text: The origin is the start of the ruler.

answer.correctWhy: 0 is the origin, where the ruler starts.

screens.caption: Drag the orange ring, then check.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 3 OF 5
screens.title: Put 3 on the line

answer.correctWhy: 3 is 3 units to the right of 0.

mistakes.reply: That is 3 units to the left. Plus numbers are on the other side of 0. Which side is that?

hints: Positive numbers are on the right of 0.

steps.text: Start at 0. Move 3 units to the right.

answer.correctWhy: 4 is 4 units to the right of 0.

screens.caption: Drag the orange ring, then check.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 4 OF 5
screens.title: Which is farther from 0?
screens.prompt: Which number is farther from 0: −7 or 5?

options.reply: 5 is 5 units from 0. Count the units from 0 to −7. Which number is farther?

feedback.correctWhy: −7 is 7 units from 0. 5 is only 5 units from 0.

hints: Count the units from 0 to each number.
A minus sign does not change the distance.

steps.text: −7 is 7 units to the left of 0.
5 is 5 units to the right of 0. 7 is more than 5.

options.reply: 6 is 6 units from 0. Count the units from 0 to −9. Which number is farther?

feedback.correctWhy: −9 is 9 units from 0. 6 is only 6 units from 0.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 5 OF 5
screens.title: The cave and the hill
screens.prompt: A cave is 30 m below sea level. A hill is 45 m above sea level. Find the distance between them in metres.

answer.correctWhy: The cave is 30 m below 0 and the hill is 45 m above 0. 30 + 45 = 75.

mistakes.reply: That is 45 − 30. The cave and the hill are on two sides of 0. Add the two distances.
A distance is not a minus number. What is the distance in metres?

hints: Draw sea level as 0 on a vertical line.
The two places are on two sides of 0. Add the distances.

steps.text: The cave is 30 m below 0. The hill is 45 m above 0.
The distance is the sum: 75 m.

answer.correctWhy: The well is 40 m below 0 and the tower is 70 m above 0. 40 + 70 = 110.

screens.label: LESSON 1.1 COMPLETE
screens.title: You can find any integer.
screens.prompt: You use the line in every later lesson:

trap.question: True or false: −7 is larger than −2, because 7 is larger than 2.

options.label: True
options.reply: −7 has the larger digit. Find −7 on the line. A point farther to the left is smaller.

feedback.correctWhy: On the line, −7 is to the left of −2. A point farther to the left is smaller.

screens.caption: Lesson 1.1 is complete.
